sentences.text: This animal belongs to the extinct group known as stomatosuchid crocodyliforms.
Scientists know the species only from the remains of their lower jaws.
One specimen, L. thaumastos, measured 838 mm in total jaw length.
Each side of the mouth held exactly 24 teeth.
Every tooth was a simple, straight spike.
Its name translates to pancake crocodile due to the skull's shallow depth.
The researchers Paul Sereno and Hans Larsson affectionately called it PancakeCroc.
Sereno and Larsson formally described the genus in 2009.
Fossils have been recovered from sites in Niger and Morocco.
L. thaumastos grew to about 6 meters long with a 1-meter flat head.
A weak symphysis indicates the animal possessed a very weak bite.
Tightly fitting teeth would have stopped fish from escaping once trapped.
Remains date to the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Cenomanian age.
The creature lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
It remains debated whether Laganosuchus had gular sacs beneath its throat, as no fossil evidence confirms or denies this feature.
